This maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since there's no history to suggest otherwise, and this is a one-shot game, I will bid exactly my value of $46 to ensure optimal expected payoff.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (paying that amount, guaranteeing profit), and you avoid overpaying when your value is lower. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, the optimal approach is straightforward truthful bidding at $28, my private value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). With independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value—bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, and bidding lower only reduces my chance of winning profitable opportunities. Since my value is $2, I will bid $2 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay a fair price if I do.
